subtitle: Global Climate & Environmental Sentinel
brief_overview: Deploy a high-resolution remote-sensing observatory into a 705 km Sun-Synchronous Low Earth Orbit (98.2° inclination) with a 16-day global repeat ground track to monitor global carbon sinks, deforestation, and climate indicators.
objectives: Achieve stable 705 km Sun-synchronous circular orbit at 98.2° inclination.
Perform global 16-day repeat multispectral imagery acquisition across 9 spectral bands.
Maintain positive electrical energy balance and thermal control during 35-minute orbital eclipse phases.
Downlink calibrated multispectral datasets to NASA Near Space Network ground stations.
engineering_constraints: LEO Drag Compensation: Upper atmospheric drag at 705 km requires periodic RCS propulsion burns to maintain constellation ground track.
Orbital Eclipse Cycles: Spacecraft spends ~35 minutes of every 99-minute orbit in Earth's shadow; Li-ion battery buffering is essential.
High Data Rate: Optical pushbroom imagers and SAR sensors generate 250+ MB/day; onboard solid-state memory is required between ground passes.
educational_context: Earth observation satellites utilize Sun-synchronous orbits so they cross the equator at the same local solar time on every pass (typically 10:00 AM descending node), providing consistent shadow angles and lighting for multi-year environmental comparisons. NASA's Earth Observing System (EOS) operates satellites like Terra, Aqua, and Landsat to monitor planetary changes.
